canonical_statement: Produce, for some integer 1<=n<=100, a triangle-free simple graph on exactly 5n labelled vertices together with at least n^2+1 pairwise edge-disjoint simple odd cycles. Every bipartite subgraph must omit at least one edge from each such cycle, so an accepted artifact needs more than n^2 edge deletions to become bipartite and is a counterexample to the unrestricted Erdős #23 conjecture. The certificate form is sufficient but not necessary for a counterexample.
success_criterion: amf.erdos23.oddcycle.v1 accepts after checking the order, canonical simple edge set, triangle-freeness, every odd cycle, and pairwise edge-disjointness of at least n^2+1 cycles. Lean closure and independent reviews remain separate.
partial_progress_criterion: Retain new verified parameter ranges, structural reductions, exact MaxCut or bipartization certificates not expressible by the edge-disjoint-cycle profile, and reusable Lean graph lemmas.
stop_conditions: The conjecture or selected finite range is superseded by current literature.
A plausible counterexample needs a different sound bipartization lower-bound certificate.
The separately approved experiment budget is exhausted.
